controller_id.d: VESC ID. Used to identify this VESC on the CAN-bus.

timeout_msec.d: Switch off the motor when no input has beed received for this amount of time. Notice that VESC Tool will send alive packets while connected, so the timeout won't occur before you disconnect VESC Tool even if the input gets disconnected.

timeout_brake_current.d: Apply brake with this amount of current after a timeout.

send_can_status.d: Send a status message on the CAN bus with a periodic interval. Useful for letting other VESCs know which VESCs are on the CAN-bus. This is required by some apps to function with multiple VESCs. The master VESC of the app does not need this option checked.

send_can_status_rate_hz.d: Rate at which CAN status messages are sent on the CAN-bus.

can_baud_rate.d: The baud rate of the CAN-Bus. Note that all devices on the bus must have the same baud rate.

pairing_done.d: Pairing done flag. If this flag is set, a bluetooth connection can only be made if the VESC Tool instance making the connection has been paired to this VESC. The pairing is done by storing the UUID of the VESC in the pairing list.

permanent_uart_enabled.d: Enable the permanent UART port (if the hardware has one). This port can be connected to e.g. the NRF51 for providing a BLE link. You may want to disable this to prevent access to your VESC over BLE.

shutdown_mode.d:
Shutdown mode for hardware that supports it (such as the VESC HD). Determines how the VESC shuts itself off, which eliminates the need for an external switch.

NOTE: Most VESCs with this feature also support push to start, which means that the VESC will switch on as soon as the motor is turned at a minimum speed.

The available modes are:

ALWAYS_OFF

The VESC power is only determined by the inverted state of the shutdown input.

ALWAYS_ON

The VESC always stays on after being powered.

TOGGLE_BUTTON_ONLY

A normally closed (NC) momentary button can be connected to the shutdown input to toggle the power on or off. The VESC will sample the button and determine whether it is pressed, which can be used to shut down after the button is released.

OFF_AFTER_x

Same as the TOGGLE_BUTTON_ONLY mode, but the VESC will shut down after X time of inactivity. This mode is useful for setups without any switch at all if the hardware supports push to start, such as the VESC HD.

can_mode.d:
CAN-bus mode.

VESC

Default VESC CAN-bus. Required for CAN forwarding and configuring multiple VESCs using VESC Tool.

UAVCAN

Basic implementation of UAVCAN. Currently needs some work.

Comm Brigde

Bridge CAN-bus to commands. Useful for using the VESC as a generic CAN interface.

uavcan_raw_mode.d:
Drive mode for the raw throttle command in UAVCAN.

Current Control

The raw command corresponds to a fraction of the configured current limit. 1.0 is maximum current forwards and -1.0 is maximum current reverse.

Current No Reverse Brake

Same as current control, but negative values only give braking and don't start the motor in the other direction.

Duty Cycle Control

Duty cycle control.

RPM Control

RPM control. Use the raw command times the maximum configured ERPM value. Negative values will run the motor in reverse. Note that this will set the value in ERPM, so the RPM will be scaled by the number of pole pairs.

uavcan_raw_rpm_max.d: Maximum ERPM for the RPM mode of the raw command.

servo_out_enable.d: Enable servo output on PPM-port when PPM-app is disabled.

kill_sw_mode.d:
Kill switch input. When this input is active the motor is disabled and optionally braking if timeout_brake_current is greater than 0. The kill switch overrides all other inputs and can be used as an emergency stop.

The following modes can be used:

Disabled

No kill switch is used.

PPM Low

The kill switch is active when the PPM input goes low.

PPM High

The kill switch is active when the PPM input goes high.

ADC2 Low

The kill switch is active when the ADC2 input goes low.

ADC2 High

The kill switch is active when the ADC2 input goes high.

app_to_use.d: The APP to use. With multiple VESC connected over CAN only the master needs to have an app to use set up. Notice that using the NRF nunchuk needs the NRF app.

app_ppm_conf.ctrl_type.d:
Off

The output is switched off regardless of the input.

Current

Current control. The output is off when the input is centered. Input less than center brakes until the motor stops, at which point it it starts in the reverse direction.

Current No Reverse

Current control. The output is off when the input is at minimum.

Current No Reverse With Brake

Current control. The output is off when the input is centered. Input less than center brakes until the motor stops, but not further.

Duty Cycle

Current control. The output is off when the input is centered. Input less than center gives negative duty cycle.

Duty Cycle No Reverse

Duty cycle control. The output is off when the input is at minimum.

PID Speed Control

PID speed control. The output is off when the input is centered. Input less than center gives negative set speed.

PID Speed Control No Reverse

Duty cycle control. The output is off when the input is at minimum.

Current Hyst Reverse With Brake

Current Hyst Reverse With Brake. The output is off when the input is centered. Input less than center brakes until the motor stops, at which point it starts in the reverse direction, but if Max dir switch ERPM is enabled it will stop the reverse when it reaches the Max ERPM for direction switch.

Current Smart Reverse

Similar to the Current No Reverse With Brake mode, but holding full brake will switch to duty cycle mode in the reverse direction when the speed is so low that not enough brake torque can be produced. This is useful when trying to stop downhill where you normally would roll forwards slowly even at full brake. Instead, the board will start to go reverse slowly in duty cycle mode if this mode is activated.

app_ppm_conf.pid_max_erpm.d: The ERPM setpoint corresponding to max input when using PID Speed Control.

app_ppm_conf.pulse_start.d: The shortest pulse length for the PPM input in milliseconds. Can be checked by enabling display and giving the minimum input.

app_ppm_conf.pulse_end.d: The longest pulse length for the PPM input in milliseconds. Can be checked by enabling display and giving the maximum input.

app_ppm_conf.pulse_center.d: The PPM input in milliseconds at which the throttle is centered. Can be checked by enabling display and leaving the throttle centered. This setting has no effect in control modes where the output is not off when the stick is centered.

app_ppm_conf.median_filter.d: Use a median filter on the decoded pulses. Will delay the signal slightly, but rejects outliers caused by noise.

app_ppm_conf.safe_start.d:
Prevent motor from starting in some unsafe conditions. Modes:

Disabled

Motor can always start.

Regular

Only allow starting the motor when the input has beed zero for long enough after boot, after configuration updates and after faults.

No Faults

Same as regular, but the motor can start directly after fault codes are cleared.

app_ppm_conf.throttle_exp.d:
Exponential gain for the throttle.

Zero (0)

Linear throttle

Negative (<0)

The throttle is softer close to 0 and increases exponentially towards full throttle.

Positive (>0)

The throttle reacts fast around 0 and decreases exponentially towards full throttle.

Increasing the magnitude of this value will increase the exponential effect. The full throttle curve can be seen in the throttle curve plot.

app_ppm_conf.throttle_exp_brake.d:
Exponential gain for the throttle.

Zero (0)

Linear throttle

Negative (<0)

The throttle is softer close to 0 and increases exponentially towards full throttle.

Positive (>0)

The throttle reacts fast around 0 and decreases exponentially towards full throttle.

Increasing the magnitude of this value will increase the exponential effect. The full throttle curve can be seen in the throttle curve plot.

app_ppm_conf.throttle_exp_mode.d:
The throttle curve mode.

Exponential

y = x^(1 + c)

Natural

y = (e^(cx) - 1) / (e^c - 1)

Polynomial

y = x / (1 + c(1 - x))

where

y: output

x: input

c: curve

The curve parameter, offsets and signs are mapped accordingly for each mode.

app_ppm_conf.ramp_time_pos.d: Positive ramping time constant. This filters the input with ramping. This constant represents the amount of secods it takes to ramp from zero to full output.

app_ppm_conf.ramp_time_neg.d: Negative ramping time constant. This filters the input with ramping. This constant represents the amount of secods it takes to ramp from full output (acceleration or braking) back to zero.

app_ppm_conf.multi_esc.d: Listen for other VESCs on the CAN-bus and send the same control commands to them. Notice that the application only has to be set up on the master VESC.

app_ppm_conf.tc.d: Enable traction control between multiple VESCs connected over CAN-bus. This is only is only used for current control modes.

app_ppm_conf.tc_max_diff.d: The ERPM difference at which the fastest motor gets swtiched off completely. If the difference in ERPM is lower than that the current to faster motors is scaled down proportionally to the difference.

app_ppm_conf.max_erpm_for_dir.d: The Max ERPM where the direction can be switched to reverse by braking 2 times.

app_ppm_conf.smart_rev_max_duty.d: Maximum duty cycle to use in smart reverse mode.

app_ppm_conf.smart_rev_ramp_time.d: Time to ramp to maximum duty cycle in smart reverse mode.

app_adc_conf.ctrl_type.d:
Off

The output is switched off regardless of the input.

Current

Current control. The output is off when the input is at minimum.

Current Reverse Center

Current control. The output is off when the input is centered. Input less than center brakes until the motor stops, at which point it it starts in the reverse direction.

Current Reverse Button

Current control with a button for reversing the throttle. The output is off when the input is at minimum.

Current Reverse Button Brake ADC2

Current control with a button for reversing the throttle. The output is off when the input is at minimum. The second ADC channel acs as a brake.

ADC_CTRL_TYPE_CURRENT_REV_BUTTON_BRAKE_CENTER

Current control with a button for reversing throttle. The output is off when the input is centered. Input less than center brakes until the motor stops, but not further.

Current No Reverse Brake Center

Current control. The output is off when the input is centered. Input less than center brakes until the motor stops, but not further.

Current No Reverse Brake Button

Current control with a button for turning the throttle into a brake. The output is off when the input is at minimum.

Current No Reverse Brake ADC2

Current control with one separate throttle connected to ADC2 for braking.

Duty Cycle

Duty cycle control. The output is off when the input is at minimum.

Duty Cycle Reverse Center

Current control. The output is off when the input is centered. Input less than center gives negative duty cycle.

Duty Cycle Reverse Button

Duty cycle control with a button on UART RX for inverting the throttle. The output is off when the input is at minimum.

PID Speed

PID speed control. The speed setpoint is mapped between 0 and the configured maximum motor speed limit.

PID Speed Reverse Center

PID speed control. The output is mapped between the minimum and maximum motor speed limits. Throttle center corresponds to 0 speed.

PID Speed Reverse Button

PID speed control with a button for reversing the throttle. The speed setpoint is mapped between 0 and the configured maximum motor speed limit, or between 0 and the minimum motor speed limit when the UART RX input is high.

app_adc_conf.voltage_start.d: Input voltage at the start of the throttle range for ADC1. Can be checked by enabling display and giving the minimum input. If Control Type is set to off while doing that the motor won't turn.

app_adc_conf.voltage_end.d: Input voltage at the end of the throttle range for ADC1. Can be checked by enabling display and giving the maximum input. If Control Type is set to off while doing that the motor won't turn.

app_adc_conf.voltage_center.d:
Input voltage at the center of the throttle range for ADC1. Can be checked by enabling display and centering the input. If Control Type is set to off while doing that the motor won't turn.

Notice that this parameter only is used for the contered control types. For the other types the voltage will always be mapped linearly between start and end.

app_adc_conf.voltage2_start.d: Input voltage at the start of the throttle range for ADC2. Can be checked by enabling display and giving the minimum input. If Control Type is set to off while doing that the motor won't turn.

app_adc_conf.voltage2_end.d: Input voltage at the end of the throttle range for ADC2. Can be checked by enabling display and giving the maximum input. If Control Type is set to off while doing that the motor won't turn.

app_adc_conf.use_filter.d: Use a low-pass filter to reject noise. This will introduce a slight delay.

app_adc_conf.safe_start.d:
Prevent motor from starting in some unsafe conditions. Modes:

Disabled

Motor can always start.

Regular

Only allow starting the motor when the input has beed zero for long enough after boot, after configuration updates and after faults.

No Faults

Same as regular, but the motor can start directly after fault codes are cleared.

app_adc_conf.cc_button_inverted.d: Invert the cruise control button. For supporting both normally-closed and normally-open buttons.

app_adc_conf.rev_button_inverted.d: Invert the reverse button. For supporting both normally-closed and normally-open buttons.

app_adc_conf.update_rate_hz.d: Rate at which the input is sampled.

app_chuk_conf.ctrl_type.d:
Off

The output is switched off regardless of the input.

Current

Current control. The output is off when the joystick is centered. Positive input gives acceleration and negative input braking. To go reverse the Z button can be used to toggle direction.

Current No Reverse

Current control. The output is off when the joystick is centered. Positive input gives acceleration and negative input braking. The reverse function of the Z button is disabled.

Current Bidirectional

Current control. The output is off when the joystick is centered. Positive input always gives forward current and negative current always gives reverse current. This means that when current is applied through 0 speed, the motor will accelerate in the other direction.

app_chuk_conf.ramp_time_pos.d: Positive ramping time constant. This filters the joystick input with ramping. This constant represents the amount of secods it takes to ramp from zero to full output.

app_chuk_conf.ramp_time_neg.d: Negative ramping time constant. This filters the joystick input with ramping. This constant represents the amount of secods it takes to ramp from full output (acceleration or braking) back to zero.

app_chuk_conf.stick_erpm_per_s_in_cc.d: The amount of ERPM per second the setpoint changes when giving full joystick input with criuse control activated.

app_chuk_conf.throttle_exp.d:

app_chuk_conf.multi_esc.d: Listen for other VESCs on the CAN-bus and send the same control commands to them. Notice that the application only has to be set up on the master VESC.

app_chuk_conf.tc.d: Enable traction control between multiple VESCs connected over CAN-bus. This is only is only used for current control modes.

app_chuk_conf.tc_max_diff.d: The ERPM difference at which the fastest motor gets swtiched off completely. If the difference in ERPM is lower than that the current to faster motors is scaled down proportionally to the difference.

app_chuk_conf.use_smart_rev.d:
Use smart reverse function. If enabled, holding full brake will switch to duty cycle mode in the reverse direction when the speed is so low that not enough brake torque can be produced.

This is useful when trying to stop downhill where you normally would roll forwards slowly even at full brake. Instead, the board will start to go reverse slowly in duty cycle mode if this mode is activated.

app_chuk_conf.smart_rev_max_duty.d: Maximum duty cycle to use in smart reverse mode.

app_chuk_conf.smart_rev_ramp_time.d: Time to ramp to maximum duty cycle in smart reverse mode.

app_nrf_conf.power.d: Transmit power or power off setting.

app_nrf_conf.retry_delay.d: Delay between retries when no ack is received. If the speed is lower than 2MBit, at least 500 µS should be used.

app_nrf_conf.retries.d: Maximum number of retries when no ack is received before giving up on the current packet.

app_nrf_conf.send_crc_ack.d: Send ACK when valid packets are received.

app_balance_conf.kp.d: P value for the PID balance loop.

app_balance_conf.ki.d: I value for the PID balance loop.

app_balance_conf.kd.d: D value for the PID balance loop.

app_balance_conf.loop_time_filter.d: Filter overshoot and correct for it.

app_balance_conf.fault_pitch.d: Angle to turn off driving (on the pitch axis).

app_balance_conf.fault_roll.d: Angle to turn off driving (on the roll axis).

app_balance_conf.fault_duty.d: Duty cycle value to trigger a safety cutoff 0-1% (This cutoff will lock the app untill another fault occurs).

app_balance_conf.fault_adc1.d: Voltage below this value will trigger a fault. To disable this switch set this value to 0. Hint: consider a pulldown resisitor!

app_balance_conf.fault_adc2.d: Voltage below this value will trigger a fault. To disable this switch set this value to 0. Hint: consider a pulldown resisitor!

app_balance_conf.fault_delay_pitch.d: Pitch fault cutoff time delay in ms.

app_balance_conf.fault_delay_roll.d: Roll fault cutoff time delay in ms.

app_balance_conf.fault_delay_duty.d: Duty cycle cutoff time delay in ms.

app_balance_conf.fault_delay_switch_half.d: Half switch cutoff time delay in ms.

app_balance_conf.fault_delay_switch_full.d: Full switch cutoff time delay in ms.

app_balance_conf.fault_adc_half_erpm.d: ERPM (absoulte value) below which a half state on the ADC switches will be considered a fault.

app_balance_conf.tiltback_duty_angle.d: Angle of rise for duty cycle tiltback.

app_balance_conf.tiltback_duty_speed.d: Speed at which vehicle is being tilted back when exceeding duty cycle limit (fast tiltback can be dangerous!).

app_balance_conf.tiltback_duty.d: Duty cycle threshold to trigger a safety tiltback (Tiltback raises the nose of the vehicle informing you to slow down).

app_balance_conf.tiltback_hv_angle.d: Angle of rise for high voltage tiltback.

app_balance_conf.tiltback_hv_speed.d: Speed at which vehicle is being tilted back when exceeding high voltage limit (fast tiltback can be dangerous!).

app_balance_conf.tiltback_hv.d: High voltage threshold to trigger a safety tiltback (Tiltback raises the nose of the vehicle to alert you). High voltage tiltback is most likely to be triggered when braking or going downhill on a full battery, sometimes resulting in a tail drag on board shaped vehicles.

app_balance_conf.tiltback_lv_angle.d: Angle of rise for low voltage tiltback.

app_balance_conf.tiltback_lv_speed.d: Speed at which vehicle is being tilted back when below low voltage threshold (fast tiltback can be dangerous and further contribute to voltage sag!).

app_balance_conf.tiltback_lv.d: Low voltage threshold to trigger a safety tiltback (Tiltback raises the nose of the vehicle informing you to slow down).

app_balance_conf.tiltback_return_speed.d: Speed at which vehicle is being returned back to normal after a tiltback condition has been cleared (should be equal to or slower than slowest tiltback speed).

app_balance_conf.tiltback_constant.d: Tiltback that will be applied above a configurable minimum ERPM. AKA nose angle adjustment, can be downwards too.

app_balance_conf.tiltback_constant_erpm.d: ERPM (absolute value) above which constant tiltback will be applied.

app_balance_conf.tiltback_variable.d: Nose angle adjustment that will be applied depending on speed, specified in degrees per 1000 erpm, applied linearly up to a maximum set in Variable Tiltback Maximum. Can be downwards (negative) too. Applies in addition to constant tiltback.

app_balance_conf.tiltback_variable_max.d: Maximum angle which variable tiltback is permitted to add (in addition to constant tiltback). Does not affect or prevent alert tiltbacks.

app_balance_conf.noseangling_speed.d: Speed at which vehicle will tilt to the desired angle.

app_balance_conf.startup_pitch_tolerance.d: Angle at which balancing will start (on the main axis). Measured in degrees from upright (0).

app_balance_conf.startup_roll_tolerance.d: Angle at which balancing will start (on the cross axis). Measured in degrees from upright (0).

app_balance_conf.startup_speed.d: Speed at which wheel will center itself on startup.

app_balance_conf.multi_esc.d: Listen for other VESCs on the CAN-bus and send the same control commands to them. Notice that the application only has to be set up on the master VESC.

app_balance_conf.yaw_kp.d: P value for yaw PID stabilization.

app_balance_conf.yaw_ki.d: I value for yaw PID stabilization.

app_balance_conf.yaw_kd.d: D value for yaw PID stabilization.

app_balance_conf.roll_steer_kp.d: Roll angle to yaw setpoint adjustment proportion. This is a constant turning speed regardless of forward travel speed. It will turn tighter at low speeds

app_balance_conf.roll_steer_erpm_kp.d: Roll angle multiplied by ERPM to yaw setpoint adjustment proportion. Scaling turn speed by erpm will give a constant turning radius at all speeds, like a normal vehicle.

app_balance_conf.brake_current.d: Breaking current to be applied when balance app is not actively balancing.

app_balance_conf.brake_timeout.d: Turn off the brake after this many seconds. It will automatically reactivate if the motor moves. 0 = Disabled.

app_balance_conf.yaw_current_clamp.d: Maximum current to be applied to yaw motions. This lets you overpower the pid traction.

app_balance_conf.kd_pt1_lowpass_frequenc.n: D term PT1 Low Pass Filter
app_balance_conf.kd_pt1_lowpass_frequenc.d: D term filter above this frequency. 0 = Disabled.

app_balance_conf.kd_pt1_highpass_frequen.n: D term PT1 High Pass Filter
app_balance_conf.kd_pt1_highpass_frequen.d: D term filter below this frequency. 0 = Disabled.

app_balance_conf.kd_biquad_lowpass.n: D term Biquad Low Pass Filter
app_balance_conf.kd_biquad_lowpass.d: D term filter above this frequency. 0 = Disabled.

app_balance_conf.kd_biquad_highpass.n: D term Biquad High Pass Filter
app_balance_conf.kd_biquad_highpass.d: D term filter below this frequency. 0 = Disabled.

app_balance_conf.booster_angle.d: Angle at which booster is applied (actually measued as absolute deviation from setpoint).

app_balance_conf.booster_ramp.d: Degrees over which booster will ramp from 0A to the Configured Current, starting at start Angle.

app_balance_conf.booster_current.d: Extra current to be applied when booster angle is reached.

app_balance_conf.torquetilt_start_curren.d: Minimum output current threshold for torque tiltback to start applying.

app_balance_conf.torquetilt_angle_limit.d: Max angle to which torque tiltback will tilt.

app_balance_conf.torquetilt_on_speed.d: Max speed at which torque tiltback will tilt to the desired angle (tilt will be slower if current increases slowly).

app_balance_conf.torquetilt_off_speed.d: Max speed at which torque tiltback will release to the desired angle back to 0 (tilt will be slower if current decreases slowly).

app_balance_conf.torquetilt_strength.d: How much tiltback should be applied based on output current.

app_balance_conf.torquetilt_filter.d: Biquad Low pass filter on the current used for calculating the torquetilt. This smooths out spikes in the current, and prevents torquetilt from being twitchy.

app_balance_conf.turntilt_strength.d: How much tiltback should be applied based on the sine of the roll angle. A strength value of N will give N degrees of tiltback when the vehicle is rolled to 90 degrees.

app_balance_conf.turntilt_angle_limit.d: Max angle to which turn tiltback will tilt. This wont change the power curve, only stop it at the limit.

app_balance_conf.turntilt_start_angle.d: Min angle threshold to apply turntilt. Similar to a deadzone, except after reaching the angle, it will apply as if it started from 0.

app_balance_conf.turntilt_speed.d: Max speed at which turntilt will tilt to the desired angle (tilt will be slower if roll angle increases slowly).

app_balance_conf.turntilt_erpm_boost.d: Increase the strength based on ERPM. Boost percent is added linearly from 0 erpm (0% boost) to max erpm (Full configured boost % is applied).

app_balance_conf.turntilt_erpm_boost_end.d: ERPM (absolute value) to end boosting the turn tilt effect, above this erpm there will be constant boost % (at your configured boost %).

app_pas_conf.ctrl_type.d:
Off

The output is switched off regardless of the input.

Cadence

Cadence control. The output is proportional to the pedalling speed, off when there is no pedalling.

Constant Torque

Constant Torque control. Pedalling provides constant output, off when no pedalling. Suited for gearless setup.

app_pas_conf.sensor_type.d:
Quadrature

This interface provides 2 signals that can be decoded to know the pedalling direction (forward of backwards).

app_pas_conf.pedal_rpm_start.d: Pedal RPM at which the assist starts. Below this value the output current is zero.

app_pas_conf.pedal_rpm_end.d: Pedal RPM at which the assist stops increasing. Above this pedal speed the assist output will stay at its maximum.

app_pas_conf.magnets.d:
How many magnets the PAS sensor assembly has. 24 magnets would provide 24 pulses per pedal revolution.

12 and 24 magnet setups are typical.

app_pas_conf.use_filter.d: Use a low pass filter in the PAS input signal

app_pas_conf.current_scaling.d: Maximum PAS output current will be limited to this percentage of the global output current.

app_pas_conf.ramp_time_pos.d: Positive ramping time constant. This filters the PAS input with ramping and represents the amount of secods it takes to ramp from zero to full output.

app_pas_conf.ramp_time_neg.d: Negative ramping time constant. This filters the PAS input with ramping and represents the amount of secods it takes to ramp from full to zero output.

app_pas_conf.update_rate_hz.d: Frequency at which the PAS control loop is executed

imu_conf.type.d: IMU type. The internal IMU is only available if the hardware supports it. External IMUs can be connected to the SDA and SCL pins. If using an external IMU, make sure that no app that uses the same pins is selected.

imu_conf.mode.d: Use the Madgwick or Mahony AHRS filter.

imu_conf.sample_rate_hz.d: IMU sample rate. Higher sample rates use more CPU cycles, but perform better.

imu_conf.accel_confidence_decay.d: This factor sets how fast the accelerometer confidence will be decreased if the acceleration vector differs from 1.0.

imu_conf.mahony_kp.d: KP for Mahony filter. Decides how much the accelerometer is used for attitude estimation. Increasing this value helps against gyro offsets, but makes the output noisier.

imu_conf.mahony_ki.d: KI for Mahony filter. Integrates gyro offsets over time.

imu_conf.madgwick_beta.d: Beta for Madgwick filter. Decides how much the accelerometer is used for attitude estimation. Increasing this value helps against gyro offsets, but makes the output noisier.

imu_conf.rot_roll.d: Roll rotation of IMU. Can be adjusted if the IMU is not aligned with the vehicle.

imu_conf.rot_pitch.d: Pitch rotation of IMU. Can be adjusted if the IMU is not aligned with the vehicle.

imu_conf.rot_yaw.d: Yaw rotation of IMU. Can be adjusted if the IMU is not aligned with the vehicle.
